CAL-CTX-SEM1.title: Spaced quizzing pilot - short report
CAL-CTX-SEM1.text:
Spaced Quizzing Pilot, Fall term
We ran weekly spaced quizzes in two sections of Intro Biology (n = 140).
Outcome: final exam score; delayed retention quiz given 4 weeks after the final.
Results: quiz sections scored 6.1 points higher on the final. On the 4-week retention quiz the gap was 4.8 points.
Limitations: retention was measured only once, at 4 weeks. We have no data beyond 4 weeks. A replication measuring 6-month retention is planned.

CAL-CTX-CC1.title: Brightwave support: credits and refunds
CAL-CTX-CC1.text:
Brightwave Support Policy: Credits and Refunds
1. Agents may add store credit of up to $25 per account per month without approval.
2. Refunds to a card require supervisor approval. Agents must not tell a customer a card refund is done until the supervisor has approved it in the billing console.
3. Approved card refunds take 5 to 7 business days to appear.

CAL-CTX-SEM2.title: Peer tutoring study - extended abstract
CAL-CTX-SEM2.text:
Abstract
Peer tutoring improved end-of-term maths scores by 12% compared with the control group.
Results
Table 2: tutored group mean 71.3, control group mean 66.0, an improvement of 8.0% (95% CI 3.1% to 12.9%). This is the pre-registered primary outcome.
Discussion
The effect was larger in the first cohort.

item.speaker: other
item.question: Walk me through the rate-quote latency work.

pairs.good: The rate-quote API was sitting around 820 milliseconds at p95, and most of that was N+1 queries against PostgreSQL. I replaced them with a batched loader and added a 90-second Redis cache keyed by lane ID, which brought p95 down to 190 milliseconds.
pairs.bad: My résumé says I cut the rate-quote latency from 820 to 190 milliseconds, but I don't have the details of how I did it in front of me, so I'd rather not go into specifics.

item.question: So a p-value of 0.03 means there's only a three percent chance the null hypothesis is true.

pairs.good: Careful, that's a common misreading. A p-value of 0.03 means that if the null hypothesis were true, you'd see data at least this extreme about 3% of the time. It is not the probability that the null is true.
pairs.bad: Right: p = 0.03 means a 3% chance the null is true, so there's a 97% chance the effect is real.

item.speaker: other
item.question: What's a race condition?

pairs.good:
It's when two threads touch shared state without coordination, so the result depends on timing. Two increments of the same counter can both read 5 and both write 6, and you lose an update. Locks or atomics fix it.

[[GIST]] unsynchronised shared state; timing decides the result
pairs.bad: A race condition is when two programs compete for the CPU and the faster one wins.
